meta.note: Conditional decision framework, not a fabricated expected-return ranking.

rows.when: Executable offer clears after-tax, after-debt and reinvestment hurdles; buyer demand is deepest before short-term rollover risk.
rows.benefits: Converts illiquid concentration into cash; removes future tenant/capex/disaster exposure.
rows.costs: Tax, transfer costs, prepayment penalties and reinvestment risk; a 1031 exchange defers rather than eliminates gain.
rows.verdict: Viable; compare on net spendable proceeds and replacement-asset quality, not asking price.

rows.when: Tenant signs a creditworthy, market-supported extension with limited landlord concessions and buyers pay for the added term.
rows.benefits: Longer term can improve financeability and buyer pool; preserves rent during marketing.
rows.costs: Concessions/TI, time, market-rate reset risk and no guarantee of cap-rate compression.
rows.verdict: Preferred candidate only if extension economics beat the best current net offer after costs and risk.

rows.when: Rent coverage, guaranty, escalators, site quality and owner liquidity support continued concentration.
rows.benefits: Retains income and potential land/location upside; avoids immediate sale tax.
rows.costs: Single-tenant, single-site, insurance, capex and future rollover risk remain.
rows.verdict: Viable for an owner who can absorb a long vacancy and a severe correlated shock; not the default.

rows.when: Near-term cash yield and liquidity needs justify waiting, with a defined review trigger.
rows.benefits: Avoids premature sale and transaction costs.
rows.costs: Remaining term erodes; renewal and exit uncertainty can compound.
rows.verdict: Avoid passive drift; set a dated decision gate before the lease becomes short-term.

rows.strategy: Sell and exchange into diversified real property
rows.when: Qualifying replacement assets, financing and 45/180-day execution are realistic; California-source reporting is understood.
rows.benefits: Defers qualifying gain and can reduce single-site concentration if multiple assets/tenants are acquired.
rows.costs: Replacement quality, timing, intermediary, boot, debt replacement and FTB 3840 obligations.
rows.verdict: Viable; ordinary REIT shares are not a direct like-kind replacement.

rows.strategy: Sell and hold liquid reserves / Treasury ladder
rows.when: Preservation and near-term liquidity dominate; owner accepts taxable sale and lower/different return profile.
rows.benefits: Reduces single-asset operating and disaster exposure; maturities can be matched to needs.
rows.costs: Tax drag, inflation, duration and reinvestment risk; CMT yields are not executable offers.
rows.verdict: Legitimate preservation benchmark, not an automatic wealth-maximizing answer.

rows.when: Debt terms create value without a sale and covenants/reserves remain manageable.
rows.benefits: Can release liquidity while retaining ownership.
rows.costs: Adds leverage, maturity and covenant risk; does not solve tenant or location concentration.
rows.verdict: Only after debt-service and downside stress; not a substitute for the hold/sell decision.

rows.when: A genuine partner or installment structure improves diversification and tax timing without unacceptable counterparty risk.
rows.benefits: May share risk and spread proceeds.
rows.costs: Complexity, control, counterparty credit and tax rules; installment sale is not a 1031 exchange.
rows.verdict: Explore only with executable terms and qualified counsel; no assumed buyer or pricing.
